'''Ernesto A. Medina''' is an ecologist specializing in plant physiology when adapting to the changing environment. He is an elected international member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], and is an adjunct professor at the Center for Applied Tropical Ecology and Conservation (CREST-CATEC).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=Research Gate Ernesto Medina |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ernesto_Medina |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191228150635/https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ernesto_Medina |archive-date=28 December 2019 |access-date=15 Dec 2020 |website=}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Medina was born on July 27, 1938, in [[Maracaibo]], Venezuela.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Medina |first=Ernesto |date=2015 |title=Curriculum Vitæ |url=https://twas.org/sites/default/files/2015_cv_emedina.pdf |access-date=2024-04-07 |website=TWAS Directory}}</ref> After receiving his undergraduate degree in biology at the [[Universidad Central de Venezuela]], he went to Stuttgart, Germany, where he completed a Ph.D. in agronomy at the [[University of Hohenheim]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=Bulletin of the Ecological Society of America, Vol.69, No.1 (Mar.1988), p.30-31. Courtesy of JSTOR |url=https://www.esa.org/history/Awards/bulletin/honorary1987me.pdf |access-date=15 Dec 2020 |website=}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
He was assistant professor at the [[Central University of Venezuela]], and joined the Department of Ecology at the [[Venezuelan Institute for Scientific Research|Venezuela Institute for Scientific Research]] (IVIC)<ref name=":1">{{Citation|last1=Lugo|first1=Ariel E.|chapter=Mangrove Forests|date=2020-05-19|chapter-url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9780429441004-12|title=Coastal and Marine Environments|pages=117–133|location=Boca Raton|publisher=CRC Press|doi=10.1201/9780429441004-12|isbn=978-0-429-44100-4|access-date=2020-12-15|last2=Medina|first2=Ernesto|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Venezuelan Institute for Scientific Research|url=https://www.researchgate.net/institution/Venezuelan_Institute_for_Scientific_Research/department/Centro_de_Ecologia/members|access-date=15 Dec 2020|website=}}</ref> in 1970.{{Citation needed|date=June 2024}}

Since 2013, he held a position as adjunct professor at the Center for Applied Tropical Ecology and Conservation (CREST-CATEC) where he continued his research on plant physiology.{{Citation needed|date=June 2024}}

== Fields ==
Medina focuses on the study of plant populations and their environmental variables, particularly nutrient availability in natural ecosystems.  His research includes the study of how a changing environment can affect [[photosynthesis]], [[Plant respiration|respiration]], and nutrient uptake during various plant developmental stages. He studies how the plant community is affected by industrial pollution, change in land use caused by agriculture, pasture, lumbering and fire management, and he applies his findings in the area of global change research. His current research focuses on plant productivity responses to salinity, drought, and nutrient availability in coastal wetlands.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Ernesto Medina |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/ernesto-medina-nv7ogq/ |access-date=2020-12-15 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
He holds an honorary membership in the [[Ecological Society of America]] supported by letters from P. D. Coley, T. A. as well as the international membership in the National Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ernesto Medina – NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/ernesto-medina-nv7ogq/ |access-date=2026-04-02 |website=nasonline.org |language=en-US}}</ref> He was one of the inaugural Fellows of the Ecological Society of America, elected in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESA Fellows |url=https://esa.org/about/awards/fellows-program/esa-fellows/ |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=Ecological Society of America}}</ref>

His honors also include [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] (1986)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ernesto Medina |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Guggenheim Foundation |language=en}}</ref> and a [[Lorenzo Mendoza Fleury Science Prize]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last1=Stanford |first1=©Copyright Stanford University |last2=California 94305 |title=Search Results |url=https://www.stanford.edu/search/ |access-date=2020-12-15 |website=Stanford University |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Public engagement ==
In 1970, he did postdoctoral research at the [[Carnegie Institution for Science|Carnegie Institution]] (Stanford, California) on the photosynthesis of plants.

In 1979, Medina was a guest at both the [[Australian National University]] and [[Stanford University]] (USA).

Medina has also participated projects with [[Man and the Biosphere Programme|MAB]], INTECOL, SCOPE (Simons Collaboration on Ocean Processes and Ecology), [[Organization of American States|OAS]], and [[FAO]]. He has helped establish a school of plant ecology in Venezuela by training 27 students through IVIC and the Universidad Central de Venezuela.<ref>{{Cite web|title=1998 Salt and Water Stress in Plants Conference GRC|url=https://www.grc.org/salt-and-water-stress-in-plants-conference/1998/|access-date=2020-12-15|website=www.grc.org}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Medina is married to Elvira Cuevas.<ref name=":5" />
